_comment: Backdrops for the journey events, cut from Kenney's CC0 Roguelike Modern City pack. Same approach as props.json: a scene is a grid of tiles from one sheet, stitched and scaled up. Nothing here is drawn by hand or generated - every pixel comes from the vendored pack. Render a labelled index to pick coordinates with: python.exe tools\art\sheet_grid.py kenney/roguelike-modern-city/Tilemap/tilemap.png --cols 0 36 --rows 0 27 --out art-source/working/city_grid.png
_licensing: Kenney Roguelike Modern City 2.0, CC0 (public domain), per its own License.txt. No attribution required; credited anyway in LICENSES.md.
_geometry: Each scene is 20 tiles wide by 12 tall. At 16px and scale 6 that is 1920x1152, which covers the 1920x1080 design resolution with room to pan. Rows are top to bottom. null leaves a tile transparent so a lower layer shows through.
_bands: Most scenes are built from three horizontal bands: a wall or sky band at the top, a detail band (windows, doors, shopfronts) in the middle, and a ground band at the bottom. The band helpers below are expanded by build_journey_scenes.py so a scene only has to name them.
_props: Single tiles dropped on top of a band. Coordinates are (column, row) on the sheet.

SC-HOME-NIGHT._note: A room with one window and a paraffin heater. Where you are born, and where the offer letter is read years later.

SC-HOME-DAY._note: The same room in daylight. Reused deliberately: the journey returns to one room and it is never different.

SC-COURTYARD._note: Walled courtyard, a tree, fruit. The only scene in the set with nothing to lose.

SC-STREET-DAY._note: The four streets a bicycle makes reachable, and the junction at the end of them.

SC-CLASSROOM._note: Forty children, one decision made in nine seconds.

SC-EXAM-HALL._note: The konkur. Rows and rows of the same desk.

SC-BARRACKS._note: Where the card is issued, which is not about the army.

SC-CAMPUS._note: A list taped to a wall. Later, the same wall, and the name on the certificate is now a flag.

SC-OFFICE._note: Cash in an envelope, counted twice because that is polite.

SC-AIRPORT._note: Departures. Used for the easy trip and, much later, for the visit that never happens.

SC-AIRPORT-SEC._note: The side of the hall the four letters send you to.

SC-CONSULATE._note: A counter, a window, and a queue that starts outside. Used for both the Turkish registration and the passport surrender.

SC-REGISTRY._note: Where your name is written down one letter wrong, permanently.

SC-BANK._note: A compliance decision arriving at a counter staffed by somebody who did not make it.

SC-CHOI-BOOTH._note: The counter itself. One booth, one officer, a line behind you that can hear everything. The room was built to carry sound toward the queue.

SC-CHOI-BACKROOM._note: Secondary inspection. Bolted chairs, no clock, a fraud helpline poster in four languages and none of them yours. Two hours of nothing happening to you on purpose.

SC-CHOI-DESK._note: Where the refusal is delivered. His desk, his folder, his monitor turned a few degrees - not enough to read, only enough to show you that turning it is his to do.

SC-DESK-NIGHT._note: Two sentences in an email, read at a desk at night.

SC-PEARSON._note: US preclearance at Toronto Pearson. Standing in Canada, at a counter that is legally the United States. The boss arena; dressed but not yet used.
